This pathway ultimately leads to the interaction with SCCH-26, a cell line that may be affected by the downstream effects of trans-urocanic acid. The evidence suggests that Nifurpirinol may modulate the activity of this G-protein subunit, potentially altering the signaling pathways that regulate cellular responses in SCCH-26. The integration of these relationships implies that Nifurpirinol could influence cellular processes in SCCH-26 through the trans-urocanic acid-G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-2 axis, although the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
